title: Guide - Calming an Anxious Heart - Name the worry

parts.style: warm, gentle welcome, steady and unhurried
parts.text: Welcome to Calming an Anxious Heart. <short pause> This practice is called Name the Worry. <short pause> If your thoughts are loud right now, you don't have to quiet them before you begin. <short pause> You can come with all of them.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Wherever you are, let yourself be supported. <short pause> Feel your feet, or your back, or the weight of your hands. <short pause> Look gently around you, and notice one thing that is simply still. <short pause> A wall... a cup... the corner of a window. <short pause> Let your breath out, without hurrying it.

parts.style: gentle, a soft smile in the voice, illustrating
parts.text: Worry rarely arrives one thought at a time. <short pause> A bill becomes the whole month. <short pause> A short message becomes a broken friendship. <short pause> A small pain becomes the worst news you can imagine. <short pause> Soon it is hard to say what is wrong... <short pause> only that everything feels wrong.

The Bible makes room for a mind like that. <short pause> In Psalm ninety-four, someone who feels their foot slipping tells God the truth about what is happening inside them. <short pause> These are their words, from verse nineteen.
In the multitude of my thoughts within me thy comforts delight my soul. <long pause>

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: The multitude of my thoughts. <short pause> A crowd of them. <short pause> And notice where God's comfort arrives. <short pause> It doesn't wait outside until the crowd has gone home. <short pause> It comes right into the middle of it.

So let's look at the crowd kindly, and find just one face in it. <short pause> What is the worry that is nearest to you right now? <short pause> It doesn't have to be the biggest, or the most sensible. <short pause> Only the one that is here.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Try putting it into a few plain words. <short pause> I am worried that... <short pause> and let yourself finish the sentence silently. <short pause> You don't need to explain it, or defend it. <short pause> Say it once more, a little more slowly. <short pause> I am worried that...

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Now notice where that worry lives in your body. <short pause> Perhaps in your chest. <short pause> Your throat. <short pause> Your stomach. <short pause> Your shoulders. <short pause> You don't have to make it leave. <short pause> Rest a hand there if you like, as you might with someone you love... <short pause> and let that place be cared for.

Next, gently separate what you know from what you fear. <short pause> There may be something true here, something that does need your care. <short pause> And there may be a story your mind has added, about how it all ends. <short pause> You can say to yourself... <short pause> this part I know. <short pause> And this part, I don't know yet.

Not knowing yet is uncomfortable. <short pause> But it is different from knowing the worst. <short pause> And there is no part of it, the known or the unknown, where God is absent. <short pause> You have named one worry in His presence. <short pause> You are not alone with it now.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: Hear the verse once more, and put your own worry inside it. <short pause> In the multitude of my thoughts within me... <short pause> even this thought... <short pause> thy comforts delight my soul.

Let's pray. <short pause> God of all comfort, <short pause> You know the worry I have just named, and the ones I haven't found words for. <short pause> Show me what is mine to care for today. <short pause> Stay with me in what I cannot know yet. <short pause> And if this is too heavy to carry alone, give me courage to tell someone who can help. <short pause> Amen.

When the crowd gathers again, you don't need to answer every voice. <short pause> Find one worry, and call it by its name. <short pause> Then remember who is standing there with you. <short pause> Go gently.
